chapter: On the road, James Brown and the 1956 crash
title: Hospital stitches and lost teeth, with the anniversary on the ward
summary: Their anniversary passes in the hospital, a doctor's lip repair draws admiring staff, and Cobb lost six teeth and more since.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: So you -- after your previous experiences you must have been (inaudible) got it in for you, I should think.
figure you must have been thinking somebody's got it in for you.
What was your sort of mental attitude (inaudible) at this time?

Well, you know, after I told you I went in for my second operation, and I was better then, and I was running into this (inaudible) nothing bothered me anymore. Our anniversary was the 29th of April, and we had talked about and discussed what we were going to do on our anniversary, where we were going to be. I said, 'We'll discuss it.'

So we had the accident on April 23rd. There wasn't no discussion. We knew where we were then, in the hospital. Friends came up from New York to visit us on our anniversary, and I'm laying up there with my teeth out, lips so -- a Chinese doctor sewed me up. Everybody in that hospital come to see that job. He did a beautiful job.

And doctors was coming in and, 'Oh, beautiful.' I didn't know what the hell they was talking about. What's beautiful? Beautiful I had the accident?

(Laughter)

It still had stitches in it. And the nurse would tell me they're talking about the job. See, your lips were cut open. I said, 'Yes, I remember that vaguely. I could stick my tongue through.'
Arnett, did that bother your embouchure? (inaudible). Got all that strength back? Well, he did do a good job.
I tell you, every doctor in the hospital come to see his job.
What about you -- had you lost your teeth then?

I lost three up and three down. Of course, I've lost more since then because, see, my bone from my jaws was damaged, and all my X-rays show dark spots. They say, 'You may have to lose many teeth. But said, if they don't bother you, don't bother it.' And I have n't lost many since then, and I might have to have all my top ones taken out now. But that's all right. I'd rather do that than to have problems.
